business_problem: However, in a competitive landscape, it’s not enough for a blockchain to be “fast and cheap,” according to Seg Rashid, Head of AI and Developer Relations at Sonic Labs. The company recognized that to sustainably attract Web3 developers, it needed to shift its focus to simplifying development with AI resources. Before adopting cloud solutions, system scalability and limited flexibility were major bottlenecks.
solution_summary: To manage this data stream, Sonic Labs built a robust, cloud-native data pipeline on Google Cloud for analysis. The architecture uses Google Kubernetes Engine for orchestration, Cloud Pub/Sub for scale ingestion, Dataflow for transformation, and BigQuery as its enterprise data warehouse. The same AI principles power internal workflow orchestration. The team uses to process unstructured tech support logs and other submissions. The large context window of Gemini models drastically reduces engineering time by eliminating the need to build complex data pre-processors. It then employs its structured output feature to instantly transform the raw data into nicely formatted, actionable tech support tickets, saving time for support staff and streamlining information handover.

data_flow: Source data is captured through Cloud Pub/Sub, stored or unified in BigQuery, Cloud Storage, processed with Vertex AI, orchestrated via Google Kubernetes Engine, Cloud Composer, and surfaced through Gemini
business_outcome: Enables functional dApp development from concept to launch in 15 minutes with Gemini; models in Vertex AI; Full availability blockchain operations on Google Cloud during market disruptions; Eliminates manual pre-processing of support logs with Gemini 2.5 Pro.
